title: How to fix a car scratch at home: a plain-English guide
subtitle: Work out how deep the scratch is, pick the right product and avoid the mistakes that make it worse.
excerpt: Work out how deep the scratch is, pick the right product and avoid the mistakes that make it worse.
shortAnswer: Most light scratches only need a touch-up pen and a clear coat. If your fingernail catches in the scratch, it's through the clear coat and needs more than polish.

steps.title: check how deep it is
steps.content: Run a fingernail across the scratch. If it doesn't catch, it's in the clear coat and polish may remove it. If it catches, you're into the colour layer or deeper.

steps.title: clean and prep
steps.content: Wash the area, dry it fully and wipe with a prep solvent. Paint won't bond to wax or road film.

steps.title: pick the right product
steps.content: For chips and fine scratches a touch-up pen is the quickest fix. See our roundup of the best touch-up paint pens for ranked options.

steps.title: apply in thin layers
steps.content: Dab, don't brush. Let each layer dry, then add clear coat. Thin layers look better than one thick blob.

commonMistakes: Applying in direct sun or on a hot panel.
